related_questions.question: What neurotransmitter is involved in depression?
Is depression low dopamine or serotonin?

text_blocks.snippet: Depression is a complex mental health condition that involves an imbalance in several neurotransmitters in the brain. Some of the key neurotransmitters implicated in depression include:

list.title: Serotonin:
list.snippet: Known as the "feel-good" neurotransmitter, serotonin regulates mood, sleep, and appetite. Reduced serotonin levels are associated with depression.

list.title: Norepinephrine:
list.snippet: This neurotransmitter plays a role in attention, focus, and arousal. Low levels of norepinephrine can contribute to feelings of lethargy and depression.

list.title: Dopamine:
list.snippet: Dopamine is involved in motivation, reward, and pleasure. Abnormally low dopamine levels can lead to decreased motivation and feelings of hopelessness.
